subject: Allocation of Defence Obligations and Litigation Handler in MSA + Order Form
messages:
From: Oliver Graves <oliver@novumtech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@novumtech.com>
Date: 2028-06-27T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: NovumTech MSA redlines (indemnity + litigation control)

Hi Irene / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking a look. Attached is our redline to the MSA and Order Form — the primary open item for us is the indemnity section. NovumTech needs: (1) defend-and-control for third-party IP claims arising out of outputs our users receive from the service, (2) a procedure for notice/evidence sharing, and (3) clarity on whether Redwood will accept subrogation/insurance offsets.

We understand Redwood's position on limiting exposure; NovumTech's legal team is asking that any carveouts for customer-provided content be explicit and that Redwood's obligation not be negated by open-source dependencies introduced by models.

Can you confirm which of these items Redwood will consider and share any counterlanguage? We're on a tight procurement timeline and would like to finalize commercial terms this week if possible.

Attachments: NovumTech_MSA_redline_v3.docx, evidence_checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Oliver
VP Strategic Partnerships
NovumTech
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-27T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovumTech MSA redlines (indemnity + litigation control)

Oliver — thanks for the redline and the checklist. Looping in Kimberly from Legal and Marissa from Sales so we can coordinate legal positions and commercial tradeoffs. Ben is CC'd for ops so we can scope evidence/forensics turnaround times.

High level from Product/Contracts: Redwood is open to a defend-and-control approach for third-party IP claims, but with narrow scope and reasonable cooperation from NovumTech. Our typical positions:
- Redwood defends claims alleging that the model or our service (excluding customer content) infringes third-party IP, provided customer: (a) gives prompt notice, (b) provides evidence in our requested format, and (c) does not materially prejudice Redwood's defense.
- Customer controls claims arising from Customer Content, customer-provided prompts, or outputs that reproduce customer-supplied materials.

Kimberly — could you propose specific language that reconciles our defend/control wanting to keep operational control, while giving NovumTech the comfort they need for user-facing outputs? Marissa — if we need to soften legal exposure, what commercial levers do you want to deploy (cap, insurance requirement, escrow)?

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for tomorrow to align.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Oliver Graves <oliver@novumtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-27T12:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovumTech MSA redlines (indemnity + litigation control)

Oliver / team — technical/legal read below. I've attached an evidence checklist and proposed indemnity paragraph (see attached doc). High-level positions and recommended compromise: 

1) Scope: Redwood will defend-and-control third-party claims that allege infringement based solely on the operation of our hosted model/service and the outputs generated where such outputs are not: (i) Customer Content, (ii) reproductions of Customer Content, or (iii) claims based on open-source model components beyond Redwood's control unless the claim arises from a trained model artifact we produced specifically for NovumTech.

2) Cooperation & notice: Customer must provide prompt written notice, preserve relevant system logs, prompt user-level artifacts (where available), and permit Redwood to control counsel selection and settlement decisions. We will keep Customer reasonably informed and will not settle to the Customer's material detriment.

3) Insurance & cap: We propose requiring Customer to maintain commercially reasonable insurance for third-party claims and apply a mutual liability cap tied to annual contract value (ACV). For defend-and-control claims covered by Redwood, propose a cap of 2x ACV with an insurance requirement of $5M per occurrence for larger deals.

4) Subrogation / offsets: Redwood will accept insurance offsets but will not permit substitutions that leave Redwood without recourse against an at-fault third-party.

5) Evidence & timelines: See attached evidence_checklist.xlsx — we need sequence logs, generation traces, prompt history, and any user-submitted content that led to the allegedly infringing output. Without those, our ability to defend is materially impaired.

I'll circulate redline language for the MSA and Order Form in the Drive link; happy to vendor-specific carveouts if NovumTech provides a short list of high-risk data flows.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: evidence_checklist.xlsx, proposed_indemnity_paragraph.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-06-28T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovumTech MSA redlines (indemnity + litigation control)

Oliver — quick note on the commercial side. If Legal needs a wider defend-and-control scope, Sales can bridge with: 
- a 2x ACV cap (as Kimberly suggested) for defendant obligations,
- mandatory $5M per-occurrence liability insurance (evidence of policy at kickoff), and
- an escrow arrangement for IP escrow or preservation on deals > $1M ACV.

If NovumTech can agree to these commercial mitigations, Revenue can recommend the concession. If you need staged concessions (e.g., 1.25x ACV for year 1, move to 2x on renewal), say so and we can propose a structured schedule.

–Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Oliver Graves <oliver@novumtech.com>

Date: 2028-06-28T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovumTech MSA redlines (indemnity + litigation control)

Thanks — some pushback from our GC. NovumTech's asks are: (a) defend-and-control for any third-party IP claim arising from user-visible outputs (even if the claim touches open-source components), (b) ability to opt for joint defense if we or our customers believe it's strategically necessary, and (c) minimal notice timing (30 days) to preserve customer remediation options.

We're open to the 2x ACV cap and $5M insurance requirement, but cannot accept a carveout that shifts all model-output responsibility back to us. For procurement, it would help to see draft MSA language that reflects Redwood's proposed carveouts and the evidence items you require so we can confirm feasibility with engineering.

Oliver
VP Strategic Partnerships
NovumTech
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Graves <oliver@novumtech.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Samira Patel <samira@novumtech.com>
Date: 2028-06-29T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovumTech MSA redlines (indemnity + litigation control) — proposed compromise and next steps

Oliver / team — thanks for the candid feedback. To keep procurement moving, here's a proposed compromise we can take to our contracts committee and to your GC: 

Proposed compromise (draft to be redlined):
- Redwood will defend-and-control third-party IP claims that allege infringement by model outputs generated through Redwood's hosted service, except where the output is a direct reproduction of Customer Content or where the claimed basis is solely the customer-provided prompt or data.
- For claims tied to open-source components, Redwood will defend if the claim arises from a Redwood-managed model variant or training artifact we delivered specifically to NovumTech; otherwise we will use a joint-evaluation approach and carve limited exposure.
- Cooperation: NovumTech must give prompt written notice, preserve generation logs/prompt history, and make available user artifacts to the extent permitted by law. If preservation or collection requires engineering support, Ben will provide a scope and estimated turnaround time.
- Cap & insurance: limit of liability for these defended claims set at 2x ACV; NovumTech must maintain $5M per-occurrence liability insurance for the contract term.
- Litigation control: Redwood will control counsel selection and settlement decisions for Redwood-defended claims, but will offer NovumTech the option of joint defense where NovumTech reasonably demonstrates a material commercial interest in control.

Next steps: Kimberly will draft redline language for the MSA/Order Form reflecting the compromise and upload to the Drive. Ben will outline the data/evidence preservation runbook and an SOW for any engineering assistance. Let's aim for a 1pm PT call tomorrow to confirm language so both legal teams can close.

If you accept the approach in principle, confirm and we'll push the redline to HubSpot and drive.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
